title: The association between in utero exposure to maternal psychological stress and female reproductive function in adolescence: A prospective cohort study.
ehr_evidence: In a large population-based pregnancy cohort study (The Raine Study) continuously followed from prenatal life through to adolescence we examined the association between the number of maternal stressful life events in both early and late gestation and subsequent ovarian and uterine function in 228 female adolescent offspring.
summary: In a prospective longitudinal cohort of 228 female adolescents from The Raine Study, maternal stressful life events during late (but not early) gestation were associated with greater uterine volume and higher ovarian antral follicle count, with no association with AMH or inhibin B.
key_findings: Exposure to one or more maternal stressful life events in late gestation was associated with greater uterine volume after multivariate adjustment (β = 0.13, 95% CI 0.04; 0.23, p = 0.01) and higher ovarian AFC (β = 0.19, 95% CI 0.02; 0.35, p = 0.03), corresponding to a 13% increase in uterine volume and 18% increase in AFC.
A linear trend for these positive associations was detected (p-value < 0.04).
No associations were found between stressful life events in early or late gestation and circulating AMH or inhibin B.
No mediating effects of maternal smoking or pre-eclampsia and no effect modification by adolescent BMI were detected (interaction p-value > 0.41).
captured_features: Number of maternal stressful life events in early gestation (reported at 18 weeks)
Number of maternal stressful life events in late gestation (reported at 34 weeks)
Ovarian antral follicle count (AFC) by transabdominal ultrasound
Maternal age, BMI, parity, and socio-economic status
Offspring height, BMI, age at menarche, and gynecological age
pathologies_diseases: Altered female reproductive function (uterine volume, ovarian reserve markers)
population: 228 female adolescents aged 14-16 years (median 15.1 years) from The Raine Study population-based pregnancy cohort in Western Australia
exposure_domain: Maternal psychological stress (stressful life events during pregnancy)
limitations: Moderate sample size with limited statistical power and risk of Type II error.
Multiple independent tests without Bonferroni correction may inflate chance findings, particularly for AFC.
Residual confounding from unmeasured pre- and postnatal factors cannot be ruled out.
Transabdominal ultrasound may be less accurate than transvaginal ultrasound, particularly in obese women.
No histological examination of ovaries to confirm primordial follicle count.
